settings.title: Settings
settings.lede: Per-provider system-instruction template — the answer-language/framing hint sent with every run. Every provider needs this for language, since none expose a real "respond in language X" API parameter. Providers with real geographic search targeting (Anthropic's web_search user_location) get that part for free — their template here should stay language-only rather than also simulating location.
settings.placeholders_hint: Available placeholders: {market_code}, {market_language}, {market_country}, {market_locale_name} (filled in from the run's market) and {persona} (the run's persona label, e.g. "person", "manager" — see /personas). In practice, only {market_language} and {persona} are usually needed here: {market_country} is handled separately and automatically wherever a provider's API offers real geographic search targeting (e.g. Anthropic's web_search user_location) — it doesn't need to be repeated in this text.
settings.empty_hint: Empty means no system_instruction is sent at all for this provider.
market.empty_state: No markets yet. Prompts need at least one market to be created.
market.delete_confirm: Delete this market? This can't be undone.
persona.label_hint: Free text, substituted directly into the system-instruction template sent to the AI provider — e.g. "person", "manager", "politician".
persona.delete_confirm: Delete this persona? This can't be undone.
ai_model.model_name_hint: Exact string passed to the provider's API — must match precisely, including any date suffix.
ai_model.cost_hint: Per-million-token price, as published by the provider. Leave empty if not yet known — never guess a price.
ai_model.delete_confirm: Delete this model? This can't be undone.
help.title: How to use SignalMap
help.lede: A walkthrough of the phase-1 workflow: client, prompt set, prompt, run.
help.overview.title: The workflow at a glance
help.overview.body: A client contains prompt sets. A prompt set contains prompts. Each prompt can be run against a model, and each run keeps its own result — nothing is ever overwritten. Every run is also checked automatically for mentions and citations.
help.clients.title: Clients
help.clients.body: A client is the organization you're tracking AI perception for. Everything else — prompt sets, prompts, runs — belongs to a client.
help.clients.name: Display name shown everywhere in the app.
help.clients.industry: Optional free-text label, e.g. "Automotive". Not evaluated anywhere — informational only.
help.clients.domain: The client's own domain, e.g. "acme.com" — used to spot it among a run's cited sources.
help.clients.notes: Optional free-text notes about the client.
help.clients.aliases_note: Alternate names (abbreviations, legal suffixes) are added on the client's detail page — they help the analysis below catch more than an exact name match.
help.prompt_sets.title: Prompt sets
help.prompt_sets.body: A prompt set is just a named folder for one client's prompts — it has no behavior of its own. Use it to group prompts that belong to the same theme or tracking wave, e.g. "Brand Perception Q3".
help.prompts.title: Prompts
help.prompts.body: A prompt is one exact question sent to an AI model.
help.prompts.text: The exact question text, sent to the model as-is.
help.prompts.market: The language/country context the question belongs to — used to classify and compare prompts across markets, and to frame the answer's language. Write the prompt text itself in that market's language too; market can also be overridden for a single run (see Running a prompt below).
help.markets_cta: Markets are managed on their own page.
help.prompts.topic: Optional label for grouping or filtering prompts later.
help.prompts.active: Inactive prompts stay in history but aren't offered for new runs.
help.running.title: Running a prompt
help.running.body: On a prompt's page, pick a model and click Run — it queries the model with web search/grounding enabled (Google Search grounding for Gemini, the web_search tool for Claude) and takes a few seconds to around half a minute depending on the model. Models are grouped by provider; a provider only appears once it has a working adapter and at least one active model. A badge below the model dropdown shows its price tier (or "Free") so you know roughly what a run costs before triggering it. The market defaults to the prompt's own, but can be changed for a single run — useful for comparing how the same question is framed for a different market without creating a second prompt. For providers with real geographic search targeting (Anthropic), changing the market changes what the search itself sees, not just the answer's language; for Gemini, only the language/framing hint changes. The run always records which market it actually used.
help.providers.title: Providers & models
help.providers.body: Each AI provider (e.g. Google Gemini, Anthropic Claude) and its models are managed on their own pages. A provider can only be renamed here, not created or deleted — a new provider always needs code (an adapter) behind it first. Models are pure data: add one, edit its price/context-window parameters, deactivate it temporarily, or delete one that was never actually used.
help.results.title: Reading a run
help.results.body: A run's page always shows what happened, whether it succeeded or failed.
help.results.success: On success: the rendered answer with detected mentions highlighted, an analysis summary, the citations the model used (domain, position, the passage they support), and the complete raw provider response in a collapsible block.
help.results.error: On failure: status is marked error and the exact error message from the provider is shown — a failed run is never silently dropped.
help.dashboard.title: Dashboard
help.dashboard.body: Aggregated view for one client over a chosen date range. Every number here is computed from the same runs, citations, and analysis results shown elsewhere in the app — nothing is stored separately for the dashboard.
help.dashboard.kpi_runs: Successful runs in the selected range. The percentage underneath compares this range to the immediately preceding period of the same length.
help.dashboard.kpi_citations: Total citations across those runs — a source cited three times in one answer counts as three, not one.
help.dashboard.kpi_domains: Number of distinct domains cited across those runs.
help.dashboard.kpi_own_rate: Share of analyzed runs where the client's own domain showed up among the citations. Computed by the mention_visibility analysis skill, which runs automatically after every run. Shows "—" when the client has no domain set, not 0%.
help.dashboard.kpi_share_of_voice: Average share of mentions the client holds against its tracked competitors. Computed by the competitive_visibility analysis skill. Shows "—" when no competitors are configured on the client's detail page.
help.dashboard.table_domain: The cited domain. A domain you've classified shows its type (Institutional, Editorial, Corporate, Reference, UGC, Other) — classification is manual, set from the table itself. The client's own domain (exact match or subdomain) gets an "Own domain" badge instead.
help.dashboard.table_citations: How many times this domain was cited across every run in the range.
help.dashboard.table_cited_in: Share of runs where this domain appeared at least once. Not the same as the citation count above — a domain cited three times in one run still only counts as one run here.
help.dashboard.table_first_last_seen: The earliest and most recent run in range that cited this domain.
help.dashboard.competitive_body: For clients with competitors tracked on their detail page, this table ranks the client and each competitor by average mention count across analyzed runs — computed by the competitive_visibility analysis skill. Not shown for clients with no tracked competitors.
help.dashboard.chart_note: The weekly chart switches between five metrics: citations, runs, own-domain rate, share of voice, and position. Weeks with no runs show 0, not a gap in the line.
help.analysis.title: Analysis
help.analysis.body: After each run, SignalMap checks whether the client is mentioned by name (or a known alias) and whether its own domain shows up among the cited sources. It's a plain text/domain match, not an AI judgment — so it's exact and reproducible. Matches are highlighted right in the rendered answer.
help.analysis.setup_note: Add the client's domain and any alternate names on its detail page — without them, only an exact match of the client's own name is checked.
help.export.title: Exporting runs
help.export.body: Every run, prompt, and client page has CSV / XLSX / JSON export buttons. CSV downloads as a .zip (runs.csv + citations.csv); XLSX is one workbook with a Runs and a Citations sheet. A prompt's export defaults to its current version only — tick "include all versions" to pull in every edited revision too. A client's export always covers every prompt set underneath it.
help.export.advanced: Add ?content=raw or ?content=full to any export URL to include the untouched provider response alongside (or instead of) the rendered answer — useful for debugging or deeper analysis, not needed for everyday use.
help.settings.title: Settings
help.settings.body: The Settings page lets you edit the locale-framing hint (system-instruction template) sent with each run, per provider. Placeholders {market_code}, {market_language}, {market_country}, and {market_locale_name} are filled in from the run's market when a run is triggered. Leave it empty to send no hint at all for that provider.
help.settings.findings_note: For why this hint exists and what it can (and can't) do,
help.language.title: Interface language
help.language.body: The EN / DE toggle in the top right switches the interface language only — not the content of your prompts or answers. The choice is remembered on this device.
help.glossary.title: Glossary
help.glossary.client: The organization being tracked. Everything else belongs to one.
help.glossary.prompt_set: A named group of one client's prompts. Organization only.
help.glossary.prompt: One exact question, plus a market and an optional topic.
help.glossary.market: The language/country context of a prompt.
help.glossary.run: One execution of a prompt against one model.
help.glossary.analysis: Whether the client shows up in an answer: named in the text, or cited via its own site.
help.glossary.citation: A source the model used, with domain, position, and the passage it supports.
